court: High Court of Judicature at Madras
facts_of_case: Wife filed for interim maintenance allowance under Section 24 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955. Trial court refused to grant relief. Wife separated from husband due to disputes and differences.

legal_principles.principle: A wife is entitled to file an application seeking interim maintenance from the respondent/husband when she is unable to eke out a living for herself.
legal_principles.held: Under Section 24 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955, when a wife is unable to eke out a living for herself, law entitles her to file an application seeking for interim maintenance from the respondent/husband.

legal_principles.principle: A welfare legislation like Section 24 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955, should be interpreted in the light of its purposes and not stultified by technical pleas.
legal_principles.held: Section 24 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955, being a welfare legislation, it requires to be interpreted in the light of the purposes for which the said provision has been brought about and the same can not be stultified by resorting to a technical plea like limitation and delay.

outcome.final_order: Civil revision petition allowed; trial court's order set aside.
